title.narrative: Addressing freshwater challenges for improving livelihood on Post Conflict Sudan

description.narrative: Since 2022, UNESCO Sudan Office has initiated projects to improve water management in regions like Red Sea State and Gadarif State, focusing on water harvesting, quality assessment, and early warning systems for floods and droughts. Key activities in 2023 included a forum on water disasters and groundwater studies amid the aftermath of the April 2023 conflict in Sudan. For 2024, webinars organized to tackle ongoing water sector challenges. A workshop in April 2025 in Port Sudan, co-organized by UNESCO, addressed water solutions and proposed the establishment of a UNESCO Chair. Sudanese representatives attended a CRIDA Workshop in Cairo in June 2025 to enhance early warning systems, and in September 2025, an online roundtable promoted youth involvement and women's empowerment in the water sector. A seminar on Disaster Risk Reduction was held in October 2025, and a Chair in Non-Conventional Water Resources was established in 2026 to address potable water access issues in Sudan. Proposed activities include cofinancing a solar-powered desalination plant in Dungonab Bay and assessing the impact of mining on water resources. There will be an evaluation of wastewater treatment in Port Sudan and supplying equipment for water quality monitoring in Khartoum State and for the UNESCO Chair in Non-Conventional Water Resources. Additional assessments involve groundwater resources in Dinder and the effect of war on water harvesting facilities in Sudan. Support will be provided for capacity development, database retrieval for the Ministry of Agriculture, and promoting integrated water resource management in the Dinder biosphere reserve. A review of the Water Policy Brief will be conducted, with webinars on water law organized. The work plan shall target cooperation between the UNESCO Chairs on Non-conventional Water Resources and Desalination. Start joint webinars and assess a major desalination plant in Port Sudan. Develop higher education curriculums, raise funds for labs, and create TVET courses for technicians.
